title: URL Encoder & Decoder - encodeURIComponent & encodeURI Tool
description: Free online URL encoder and decoder. Switch between encodeURIComponent and encodeURI modes, inspect query strings in a parameter table, and copy results.
quickAnswer: encodeURIComponent() encodes every character except A–Z, a–z, 0–9, -, _, ., !, ~, *, ', (, ). Use it for individual query-string values. encodeURI() preserves structural characters (:, /, ?, #, &, =) and is used for complete URLs. To decode, paste percent-encoded text and the tool reverses each %XX sequence to the original UTF-8 character.

commonMistakes.title: Double-Encoding
commonMistakes.description: Encoding an already percent-encoded string converts existing % characters into %25 (e.g. %20 becomes %2520). Always verify whether incoming data is already encoded before applying transformation.

commonMistakes.title: Using encodeURI for Query Values
commonMistakes.description: Running encodeURI on a parameter value leaves characters like & and + unencoded, causing server parsers to truncate or split values unexpectedly.

commonMistakes.title: Malformed Percent Sequences
commonMistakes.description: Decoding a string with a bare percent sign (such as discount=50% instead of discount=50%25) throws a fatal JavaScript URIError: URI malformed. Safe tools catch and surface this error clearly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between encodeURIComponent and encodeURI?
faqs.a: encodeURIComponent encodes all reserved punctuation characters (including &, =, ?, /, :, and #) into percent-encoded hex sequences. It is intended for encoding individual query parameter keys and values. In contrast, encodeURI preserves valid URL structure characters (;,/?:@&=+$#) and only encodes characters forbidden in standard URIs like spaces and Unicode glyphs.

faqs.q: When should I use encodeURIComponent instead of encodeURI?
faqs.a: Always use encodeURIComponent when preparing values to append to a query string (e.g., ?q=search+term or ?redirect_url=https://example.com). If you used encodeURI, symbols like & and = inside your value would be mistaken for additional query delimiters.

faqs.q: How does this tool handle '+' plus signs in query strings?
faqs.a: In application/x-www-form-urlencoded query strings, plus signs (+) commonly represent spaces. When decoding in Component mode, this tool translates both '+' and '%20' into standard space characters.

faqs.q: Is my URL or private query parameter data sent to a server?
faqs.a: No. All URL encoding, decoding, and query string table parsing run 100% locally in your web browser. Sensitive API tokens and query strings never leave your device.

faqs.q: What is the maximum URL size supported?
faqs.a: The tool supports inputs up to a 1 MB safety cap (1,048,576 characters). Live debounced processing ensures instant UI updates without lag.

how-when-to-use-the-url.li1: Passing Nested URLs in Redirects: When passing a return URL (e.g. ?returnTo=https://example.com/dashboard?tab=billing), use encodeURIComponent so the nested query parameters aren't parsed by the outer server.
how-when-to-use-the-url.li2: Fixing Broken Links with Spaces: Web browsers require valid ASCII URIs. Encode spaces as %20 (or +) and non-ASCII Unicode characters before sharing links.
how-when-to-use-the-url.li3: Debugging Webhook Payloads & Query Strings: Paste complex query strings to view every parameter neatly parsed into a structured table.
how-when-to-use-the-url.li4: Safe Form Data Encoding: Verify how input field data will be transmitted in application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST requests.

url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.p1: RFC 3986 specifies percent-encoding to represent characters in URIs outside the allowed ASCII character set. Understanding the distinction between component and full URI modes prevents broken routes and corrupted parameters.
url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.td2: Spaces are never permitted in valid URIs.
url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.td6: Delimits query parameters; must be encoded inside values.
url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.td10: Separates key and value; must be encoded inside values.
url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.td14: Begins query string; must be encoded inside values.
url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.td18: Separates path segments; must be encoded inside values.
url-encoding-specification-mode-comparis.td22: Begins fragment anchor; must be encoded inside values.
